title: Rearrange Linked List in Zigzag Order
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of length `n`, rearrange its node values in a single left-to-right pass so that the list follows the zigzag wave pattern `node[0].val <= node[1].val >= node[2].val <= node[3].val >= ...`.

To guarantee a unique output, apply the canonical single-pass procedure for index `i = 0, 1, ..., n - 2`: when `i` is even, if `node[i].val > node[i + 1].val`, swap `node[i].val` and `node[i + 1].val`; when `i` is odd, if `node[i].val < node[i + 1].val`, swap `node[i].val` and `node[i + 1].val`.

Return the head of the rearranged linked list in `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Maintain a boolean flag `expectLess` starting as `true` (meaning `curr.val <= curr.next.val` is required at even indices) and flip it at every step.
Swapping `curr.val` with `curr.next.val` when the current pair violates the required inequality never breaks the inequality already established with the previous node.

examples.explanation: A single-node list [5] trivially satisfies the zigzag condition.
